source_notes: Moderate, not ironclad, per the brief's own framing -- no single dated primary statement says 'Gastrade owns the vessel' post-closing. Chain of evidence: an offshore-energy.biz piece (27 Nov 2023, covering the vessel's Seatrium-shipyard departure) states the vessel was THEN owned by GasLog ('the Alexandroupolis, former GasLog Chelsea, is owned by GasLog, a partner in the Gastrade consortium'), consistent with GasLog owning it during the conversion phase. LNG Prime (17 Dec 2023) reports the planned sale explicitly: 'GasLog will sell this unit to Gastrade for about $265 million.' Blackridge Research's current project-profile table lists the FSRU as 'Designed, Built, Owned, and Operated | Gastrade', crediting GasLog only for the conversion/operation role. Together these two independent, current sources support a completed ownership transfer to Gastrade AE post-delivery, but neither is a single ironclad dated 'ownership closed' primary announcement -- hence yellow, not green. If a firmer post-closing primary source (SEC/bond-prospectus filing, Gastrade press release) surfaces later, upgrade to green.

source_notes: FIDYear=2022 with FIDStatus=Pre-FID is the ORIGINAL target year, now four years stale -- FID has not occurred. Three independent, current (2026) Greek trade-press sources -- energymag.gr, ypodomes.com, worldenergynews.gr -- all state Motor Oil now targets the final investment decision (FID) by the end of 2026, alongside a construction-start target of 2027. This is a genuine, well-corroborated schedule update to the TARGET year (FIDStatus stays Pre-FID; only the expected-FID-year anchor moves), analogous to a LatestPlannedStartYear slip. Companion finding: construction-start (2027) and the DESFA development-plan status question are covered in the Dioriga qa entries and the LatestPlannedStartYear update below. [ref-restore 2026-07-29: restored existing live URL(s) https://lngprime.com/europe/greece-backs-motor-oils-fsru-project/72189/ per merge-semantics rule (bot-block != dead; never drop a URL not proven dead)]

The 2023 target has unambiguously slipped (FID not yet taken, construction not started as of July 2026) -- per the planned-startup-slip elevation rule this must be staged, not left in a qa note. Powergame.gr (29 Jul 2026, Montel-sourced) is the only source giving a specific forward estimate: 'traders estimate commercial operation of the FSRU Dioriga Gas will likely start in 2028 or 2029.' I take the later/more conservative bound (2029), consistent with GEM's own already-updated LatestPlannedStartYear=2029 for the comparable/nearby Thessaloniki FSRU and with this class of Greek FSRU project historically slipping later rather than earlier. This specific 2028-2029 estimate is corroborated by only ONE source (below the usual 2-source bar) -- yellow, not green -- but it rests on strong contextual corroboration: THREE independent sources (energymag.gr, ypodomes.com, worldenergynews.gr) agree construction itself won't start until 2027 and FID is not expected before end-2026, which makes any operations date before 2028 implausible and supports the direction and rough scale of the powergame.gr estimate. Recommend the reviewer confirm with a second source if one surfaces.
